title: Comparison between Early Clinical Results of Dual-Linear and Conventional Foot-Pedal Control in Phacoemulsification
indication: Bilateral cataract (LOCS III nuclear opacity NO2-NO6), patients older than 45 years without prior ocular surgery, corneal disorders, uncontrolled glaucoma or low preoperative ECC; paired-eye design, both eyes operated by one surgeon (2.0 mm incision, pre-chop, Stellaris Elite multiple burst mode)

groups.description: Study group: dual-linear foot-pedal control (pitch for phaco power, yaw for vacuum) with adaptive fluidics
Control group: conventional pitch-only foot-pedal control with gravity infusion, contralateral eye of the same patients

exclusions.what: jcm-13-00693-t004 'Minimum' and 'Maximum' columns (C3, C4, C7, C8)
jcm-13-00693-t003 R2 endothelial cell loss at 3 months
exclusions.reason: percent loss of the same groups; the absolute ECD series is used

exclusions.what: jcm-13-00693-t006 R7 endothelial cell loss by nuclear grade
exclusions.reason: subgroups nested within the two arms with a single follow-up; the arm-level absolute series is used
same preoperative means as Table 4 R4

notes: Retrospective paired-eye contralateral study; the first operated eye was randomly assigned to one pedal control; both eyes were operated, so the contralateral eye is an operated arm, not an unoperated fellow eye.
Authors label the dual-linear eye 'study group' and the conventional eye 'control group'; dual-linear pedal control is recorded as the treated technique variant.
Patients who missed routine postoperative visits were excluded (Methods), so all 94 eyes per arm are expected at each visit; the table does not state n.
